title: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
grouping: No containers or panels. A stack of input video frames on the left forks into two parallel branches (Video tokenizer above, Latent action model below); each branch ends in a row of token bars, and the two rows merge into the Dynamics model, which leads to a stack of output frames on the right. Each module and its output tokens share one fill colour.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with black outlines and saturated fills: dark navy (Video tokenizer, white text), mustard yellow (Latent action model), coral red (Dynamics model). Tokens are flat solid rectangles in their producer's colour: tall thin navy bars for video tokens z, short yellow squares for latent actions a-tilde, each row ending in an ellipsis and a final bar. Input and output videos are overlapping stacks of real game frames with a curly brace labelled 'T frames'.
proposed_highlight: No ours/prior marking; all three modules are equal-weight saturated boxes, distinguished only by colour, and the two token rows are coloured to match the module that produces them.
lesson: Colour each module's output tokens the same as the module, so when two branches merge into one model the reader sees which representation came from which branch without a legend.
notes: venue: unverified (the PDF has no venue footer, only a 2024-2-26 date and the arXiv stamp); remembered as ICML 2024. year = arXiv preprint year. The whole figure is one embedded raster (refs crop records an image covering the entire crop), so measured.photo_share is null and the palette is taken from the whole raster, including the game frames.

arrangement.units: one unframed left-to-right strip: input frame stack, two stacked module branches with their token rows, one merging module, output frame stack
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real platformer-game frames with a curly brace labelled 'T frames'
arrangement.shared: the input frames feed both branches through one forking line

taxonomy.task: learning an action-controllable generative world model from unlabelled video

insights.structure: A fork-and-merge: one input feeds two stacked parallel modules whose outputs reconverge on a third module, so the two-branch-then-fuse structure is visible before any label is read.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are real game frames stacked with a 'T frames' brace, and both intermediate representations are drawn as token rows (tall navy bars for z, short yellow squares for a-tilde) between the module that makes them and the module that consumes them.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is singled out as new; the three modules carry equal size and saturation, separated only by hue.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with short orthogonal black arrows: one fork after the input stack, one right-angle merge of the two token rows before the Dynamics model, one straight arrow to the output frames.
insights.avoid: The two token rows merge at a bare line junction, so how z and a-tilde are combined is not drawn, and line style does not mark which branch is used only in training.

core.what: input frames fork into two stacked branches (video tokenizer, latent action model) whose token rows converge by right-angle lines on one Dynamics model

relations.form: navy token row from the upper branch and yellow token row from the lower branch join in one right-angle merge into the Dynamics model box
the Video tokenizer and Latent action model sit one above the other in two equal-width parallel branches fed by a single forking line from the input stack
one left-to-right axis: input frame stack, modules, token rows, Dynamics model, output frame stack

channels.colour: hue = which module; a module's output tokens repeat its hue (navy = tokenizer and z, yellow = latent action model and a-tilde, coral = Dynamics model)
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = module; solid bar / square = token (tall bar = video token, small square = latent action); stacked frames = video data
channels.line: one style only: thin black orthogonal arrows for data flow

quality.strengths: The core fork-and-merge is pure geometry; each colour has one meaning (module identity carried onto its tokens); both compared representations are drawn as token rows between maker and consumer; real frames as input and output; all lines short, straight and orthogonal with a single fork and a single merge.
quality.weaknesses: Space does not follow novelty: the latent action model, tokenizer and dynamics model are equal-sized boxes, so the figure does not say which part is new; the merge of z and a-tilde is a bare junction; training-only vs inference paths are not distinguished by line style; no decoding step is drawn between the Dynamics model and the output frames.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
